title: The RSI page's Landings card shows a mission's objectives settled over time when no objective has a metric
prompt:
Read web/src/rsi.ts (`RsiMission`, `RsiObjective`, `RsiLanding`, `RsiSolvedOnBase`, `chartObjective`, `metricPoints`), web/src/components/rsi/RsiView.tsx (`HistoryCard`, the Landings card), web/src/components/rsi/MetricChart.tsx and metric.ts (the ratchet chart and its empty state), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`/api/rsi`, an objective row's `solved_on_base`), and crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (`OBJECTIVE_MISSIONS`, whose `solved_on_base` rows already carry `at_ms`).

The problem, as the owner reads the RSI page after 73e3596d (lead-mac; sync/page-rsi-2026-11-11-2336.png). The Landings card, the page's largest, says "No landed measurements yet" and "The first landing records the starting baseline" for mission 4. Mission 4 has 49 of 50 objectives settled and 48 landings. The card charts the ratchet of one metric objective, but no objective of mission 4 or mission 6 names a metric: live /api/rsi has 50 and 108 objectives, 48 and 108 landings, 0 metrics. So the card is empty on both missions for good, and tells the owner that a mission which has done nearly all its work has done nothing.

Required behaviour.
(a) `/api/rsi`: an objective's `solved_on_base` carries `at_ms`, the time of the integrator's `objective.solved` record, beside `event`, `task` and `base`.
(b) A new module, web/src/rsiProgress.ts, loads with node alone (type-only imports). It exports `settledProgress(mission)`, which returns {total, settled, points}:
- `total`: the mission's objectives;
- `settled`: those whose status is solved or met;
- `points`: one per settled objective, {objective, task, at_ms, settled, on_base}. A point sits at the objective's first landing (`task` that landing's), or, for an objective solved on the base with no landing, at its `solved_on_base.at_ms` (`task` the record's, `on_base` true). Points run oldest first, ties by objective id, and `settled` counts up from 1.
With nothing settled, points are [] and settled is 0.
(c) It also exports `progressTitle(progress)`, which reads "<settled> of <total> objectives settled".
(d) The Landings card: when no objective of the mission has a metric, it charts `settledProgress` as a step line over time, titled with `progressTitle`, in place of "No landed measurements yet". Its last line names the latest point's objective and task and how long ago it was. A mission with a metric objective is charted as today.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/063.sh. The history is seeded as the store holds it and folded by `spawn_control_refold()`, and `spawn serve` answers. One objective mission's backlog holds objectives 1 to 5, none with a metric:
- task 4 lands objective 4 at -8 h, first in time though not by id;
- task 1 lands objective 1 at -7 h;
- task 2 lands objective 2 at -5 h;
- objective 3 is recorded solved on the base at -4.5 h (task 3, no landing);
- task 5 (objective 5) is in flight.
Checks:
- (1) Through `GET /api/rsi`, objective 3's `solved_on_base.at_ms` is its record's time.
- (2) Under node over that answer, `settledProgress` gives total 5, settled 4, and points for objectives 4, 1, 2 and 3 (on_base) in that order, with settled 1 to 4, at the task.landed records' and the objective.solved record's times.
- (3) `progressTitle` reads "4 of 5 objectives settled". The same mission with nothing settled gives points [], settled 0 and "0 of 5 objectives settled".
It fails with 1 on 73e3596d: `at_ms` is null, and web/src/rsiProgress.ts does not exist.

The product reason. The RSI page is where the owner sees whether a mission is moving, and for the missions that do the fleet's work its main card says nothing ever happened. Charting objectives settled over time shows the pace at a glance, and also when it stalls.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a serve.rs test that `solved_on_base` carries `at_ms`, and web/test tests for (b) to (d), including a mission with a metric objective still charted as today.
